messages:
InfraBot: PAGER: (sev=P1) KV cache eviction rate spike + arena fragmentation detected in prod-serving-us-east-1. Multiple GPU workers showing repeated OOMs and continuous-batching queue growth. Error signature: `cudaMalloc failed: out of memory` + `kv_cache slab_free_count falling to 0`. Impact: 15% increased 5xx for text-gen endpoints and several large customers reporting degraded throughput.

SRE Oncall: I see it. Tracing shows cont-batch queues ballooning on pool gpus-g1. Eviction latency skyrocketed. Rolling averages of token latency up ~220% for 90th pct.

Priya R: tagging infra/runtime -- likely allocator + KV slot fragmentation. Recent rollout 3h ago adjusted `cont_batch.max_inflight` from 16 -> 48. @Matt H did that change come via canary?

Matt H: yep that was from the dynamic-batching experiment. Canary looked ok on dev but we didn't hit prod peak QPS. Rolling it back now.

Anna K: any quick mitigation besides rollback? Customers are seeing errors in streaming responses.

DeployBot: rollback job queued: rollback/deploys/dynamic-batching -> v1.3.4 (started). ETA ~45s for canary, ~2m for full pool if no failures.

SRE Oncall: while rollback runs, can we reduce memory pressure by forcing KV prefix caching disabled for large requests? A short-term knob: `KV_CACHE_PREFIX_ENABLED=false` per-route. We can patch gateway filter for high-cost routes.

Matt H: I can push a per-route patch to disable prefix caching for /v1/generate-heavy. Command I used locally:

```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \ 
  https://console.internal/api/routes/patch \ 
  -d '{"route":"/v1/generate-heavy","overrides":{"kv_cache_prefix":false}}'
```

Matt H: pushing that now.

Priya R: good. Also engage arena compaction on the affected hosts (linux: echo 1 > /sys/devices/arena/compaction) — we have a guarded script. Will coordinate with oncall to run on two workers as canary.

SRE Oncall: please run on one worker first. We need to avoid compaction-induced latency spikes.

Priya R: running on worker gpu-12 now:

```
ssh ops@gpu-12 'sudo /usr/local/bin/arena_compact --threshold=0.6 --dry-run=false'
```

Priya R: compaction completed on gpu-12. Memory pressure reported down ~18%, no spike in tail latency yet.

Jay C: customer-impact note: customers A & C reported failures; CS is sending incident acknowledgement. ETA for customer-facing note: 30m if we don't fully resolve.

eng-runtime: adding detail — allocator histogram shows many small unusable slabs due to variable `cont_batch` increase; fragmentation worsens because KV entries are pinned in caches during longer inflight batches.

Anna K: can we temporarily throttle cont_batch concurrency globally? e.g., set `cont_batch.max_inflight=20` via runtime-config until we validate rollback.

Matt H: I can set a global override. Applying patch now.

DeployBot: config push success to config-store. Propagating to 12/12 regions. Nodes will pick up within ~40s.

SRE Oncall: monitoring. If cont-batch items drain and OOM stops, we consider this mitigated. Alert threshold: eviction-rate < 200/s and 5xx back to baseline.

InfraBot: Alert update: eviction-rate peaked at 1780/s, now 220/s after rollback + compaction + global throttle. 5xx reduced from +15% -> +3%.

Matt H: good sign. Still seeing a handful of OOMs on older hosts with stale allocator settings (jemalloc override missing). Those hosts have `LD_PRELOAD` mismatch.

Priya R: identifying hosts with stale env. Running a rolling restart of runtimes on 6 workers with stagger 30s to pick up allocator fixes.

SRE Oncall: please do 2 at a time to avoid losing capacity.

Priya R: rolling restart in progress. Commands used:

```
for host in gpu-21 gpu-22 gpu-23 gpu-24 gpu-25 gpu-26; do
  ssh ops@$host 'sudo systemctl restart redwood-runtime' && sleep 30
done
```

eng-runtime: note: also adjusting `pytorch_cudamalloc_async` flag back to `true` on affected nodes; previous experiment toggled it off and that's correlating with higher fragmentation in long-running processes.

Matt H: patched that across 6 nodes.

Jay C: customer impact update: CS has sent an initial note to customers that saw errors. We're offering a postmortem once root cause confirmed. No escalations yet.

SRE Oncall: metrics look stable for 7 minutes: eviction-rate ~180/s, 5xx ~+2%, latency 95th back to within 1.2x baseline. Recommend marking initial mitigation success. Will keep the incident open until all nodes stable for 30m.

Anna K: action items before close —
- revert dynamic-batching experiment permanently until we can simulate prod peak
- add preflight for `LD_PRELOAD` + allocator env during canary
- add a runtime guard to auto-throttle batching on sustained eviction spikes (>500/s for 60s)
- write runbook entry for arena_compact usage and safe pace

Matt H: agree. I'll open tickets and a follow-up RFC for safer batching rollout plan.

eng-runtime: please collect heap histograms and kv-slab maps from affected nodes and drop into /incident/3444123456/artifacts. Use `kv_inspect --format=json`.

Priya R: collected artifacts from gpu-12/gpu-21/gpu-23 and uploaded.

SRE Oncall: handing off to night oncall at 3444125200 (in ~21m). Night oncall, please monitor eviction-rate and OOM counts; escalate to eng-runtime if we see >5 OOMs across pool in 10m.

InfraBot: Incident P1 acknowledged. Status: MITIGATED -> Monitoring. Channel: incidents. Thread will remain open for postmortem notes.

Jay C: I'll coordinate customer follow-up and publish an acknowledgement. Will include possible root causes and ETA for postmortem.

SRE Oncall: thanks team. Closing actions: keep this thread updated if anything deviates. We'll draft postmortem template and link artifacts.

Matt H: filing ticket: RED-INC-2026-3444123456 - dynamic-batching regression -> allocator fragmentation.

Anna K: adding runbook checklist to knowledge base now.

InfraBot: AUTO: created incident ticket RED-INC-2026-3444123456 and assigned to eng-runtime, SRE, and product.

SRE Oncall: handing off. Night oncall please acknowledge when you take over.
